correctness.rationale: Annihilator classes are exactly valuation vectors in the product of chain factors; adjacency and degrees are derived coordinatewise. Leaves identify factors, leaf-neighbor degrees reconstruct each length, and all small-order exceptions are handled explicitly. The only duplicate reconstruction is the two-vertex complete graph coming from lengths {3} and {1,1}.

value.rationale: The result completes a natural information-recovery question raised by the simple compressed graph: for finite principal ideal rings it identifies exactly which chain-factor data survive graph compression and proves the previously exhibited p^3/pq ambiguity is the only chain-length failure. This is a structural classification rather than a recomputation of a small invariant.
